impact:
ISS-005 fixed the server's answer to "what day is it". This is the other half of the reported symptom and is not addressed by it.

The query client sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` with `staleTime: 10_000`. Any remount refetches, so navigating between tabs self-corrects. The gap is the app left open on the Start screen across midnight: FuelPanel stays mounted, the window regains focus without a refetch, and yesterday's totals stay on screen against today's target until something else triggers a fetch. On a phone, where the app is backgrounded rather than closed, that is the normal way to use it.

Worth being clear that this is a distinct cause from ISS-005 with the same user-visible effect, which is why it needs its own fix rather than being assumed closed: after the timezone fix, a stale cache is now the only remaining way to see a counter that did not reset.

Options, roughly in order of directness: re-enable `refetchOnWindowFocus` for the fuel queries specifically (the global default was set to avoid thrash on every screen, so a per-query override is narrower than flipping it); or have FuelPanel invalidate `["fuel","today"]` when the local calendar date changes, which is the condition actually being waited on rather than a proxy for it. A date-change check also covers the tab that is never refocused because it was never backgrounded.

Not filed as part of ISS-005 because that issue is about the day boundary being computed in the wrong zone, and this is about not asking again once it changes.
title: Fuel totals can survive local midnight in an open tab: no refetch on focus
